holes_found.description: NEW (Lens B cross-WIN consistency): WIN-061 detail_evidence states 'Because 7.83 Hz requires H_eff >= 9,579 km and H(r) peaks at 8,537 km, no averaging choice can reach the observed baseline' while WIN-029 detail_evidence opening uses 'H = c/(4f) = 299,792/(4 * 7.83) = 9,572 km' and WIN-038 detail_evidence paragraph 1 says 'the same formula WIN-029 uses to back-derive a 9,572 km ceiling from 7.83 Hz' — three WINs, two values, one calculation. Precise arithmetic c/(4 * 7.83 Hz) = 299,792,458 m/s / 31.32 s^-1 = 9,572.5 km (rounded). WIN-061's '9,579 km' is off by 7 km (~0.07%). The qualitative conclusion (H_required > H_max regardless of averaging) is unaffected — both 9,572 and 9,579 well exceed 8,537 — but the within-page numerical inconsistency is a free shot for a hostile reader: 'WIN-029 and WIN-038 say 9,572; WIN-061 says 9,579; pick one.' On the other side: rounding-level inconsistency bounces off a reader who already accepts the qualitative point, and three independent WINs converging on H_required > H_max is robust to a 0.07% error in any one. Severity stays minor; fix is a one-character edit with zero downside.
holes_found.recommendation: Decider self-apply: replace '9,579 km' with '9,572 km' in WIN-061 detail_evidence paragraph 1. One-character edit; aligns with WIN-029 and WIN-038 numerics and with precise c/(4f) arithmetic.

holes_found.description: NEW (Lens A anchor consistency): the new Timestamp Error tab parenthetical uses href='#' (hash-only, no named anchor) while every other tab cross-reference in wins.json (61 occurrences across all WINs) uses href='#named-id' with a named target. WIN-061 is the lone hash-only outlier. The parenthetical reads 'see the Timestamp Error tab' — the navigation depends entirely on the JS onclick handler. If JS fails (NoScript, CSP block, non-JS reader, copy-paste into a different context) the link degrades to scroll-to-top rather than to a section anchor. Earlier in the SAME WIN-061 paragraph the Section 2.1 cross-reference uses href='#part2' with a real anchor — so the precedent for named anchors is established within this same field. The inconsistency is intra-WIN, which is more exploitable than cross-WIN. On the other side: the onclick handler does work in the production site and the hash-only fallback degrades gracefully; naming the anchor introduces a fragile dependency on the actual id attribute of the Timestamp Error section in the rendered HTML. The fix is to point href at whatever anchor target the build pipeline uses for that tab (likely #timestamp).
